designationHistory.name: Tule Lake Bird Refuge
designationHistory.indexText: President Calvin Coolidge established the Tule Lake Bird Refuge by Executive Order 4975 on October 4, 1928, as a preserve and breeding ground for wild birds and animals.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: Tule Lake National Wildlife Refuge, About Us

American Presidency Project: Executive Order 5945, Nov. 3, 1932, Establishing the Tule Lake Wild Life Refuge, California (revokes "Executive Order No. 4975, of October 4, 1928, establishing the Tule Lake Bird Refuge")
Wikisource: Proclamation 2416, July 25, 1940 (renaming federal wildlife refuges; lists originating orders)

review.note: Year and signer confirmed; exact date, EO and earlier name from the recital in EO 5945 (Hoover, 1932), which re-established it as the Tule Lake Wild Life Refuge.

designationHistory.indexOriginal: Tule Lake National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1928 by President Calvin Coolidge “as a preserve and breeding ground for wild birds and animals.” Today it is part of a complex of six National Wildlife Refuges in the Klamath Basin that include Tule Lake, Upper Klamath, Lower Klamath, Klamath Marsh, Bear Valley, and Clear Lake, whose combined mission is to protect what remains of what once was
